# `endpoints/unauthenticated-data-access`: Endpoint reads or changes data without an authentication check

<!-- Generated by `npm run docs:rules` from the rule metadata in src/rules/. Edit only the
     hand:* regions here; everything else comes from the rule and is overwritten. -->

| Family    | Default severity | GitHub security-severity | CWE                                                                                                                                                                                |
| --------- | ---------------- | ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| endpoints | high             | 8.0                      | [CWE-306](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/306.html), [CWE-862](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/862.html), [CWE-285](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/285.html) |

Individual findings can have a lower or higher severity than the default, and each has a
confidence (high, medium or low). Both are explained below.

## What it detects

<!-- hand:detects -->

Server endpoints that read or modify data, write files, or call external services with
server credentials, without a verified authentication check:

- **Next.js:** App Router route handlers, Pages Router API routes, server actions
  (`'use server'`); Vercel functions.
- **Express and Fastify:** routes, with `app.use` ordering and Fastify plugin encapsulation
  respected.

Data access is recognised by API shape: Supabase, Firestore (client and Admin SDK), Prisma,
Drizzle, Mongoose-style models, `pg` / `mysql` `.query()`, D1 / SQLite prepared
statements, `sql` tags, `fs` writes, and SDK clients built with secrets.

Authentication is three-valued:

- **verified** (no finding): `auth()`, `getServerSession`, `currentUser`,
  `supabase.auth.getUser()` / `getClaims()`, `verifyIdToken`, `jwt.verify`, auth middleware
  earlier in the chain, or a Next.js `middleware.ts` / `proxy.ts` that authenticates and
  blocks and whose matcher covers the route;
- **weak:** only `supabase.auth.getSession()`, which does not verify the session on the
  server (lower severity);
- **unverified:** a helper whose body VibeGuard cannot inspect (low confidence).

Helpers are followed one level. A helper named like auth only counts after its body is
checked. Severity is highest for writes with a privileged (service-role / admin) client.

<!-- /hand:detects -->

## Why it matters

Route handlers, API routes, server actions and Express/Fastify routes are public URLs: anyone can call them directly, without your UI. This one reaches the database (or a privileged SDK) and VibeGuard found no authentication check in the handler, its middleware, the helpers it calls, or a Next.js middleware that covers it. Hiding a button in the UI is not access control. Server actions in particular are POST endpoints that anyone can invoke.

## Messages

What a finding from this rule says (parameters in braces):

- {endpoint} modifies data with a privileged client ({api}) and has no authentication check: anyone can call it.
- {endpoint} modifies data ({api}) and has no authentication check.
- {endpoint} reads data with a privileged client ({api}), bypassing Row Level Security, and has no authentication check.
- {endpoint} reads data ({api}) with no authentication check. Confirm the data is meant to be public.
- {endpoint} calls an external service with your server credentials ({api}) and has no authentication check: anyone can spend your quota or act with your account.
- {endpoint} reaches data ({api}) after only supabase.auth.getSession(), which reads the session cookie without verifying it. Use getUser() (or getClaims()) on the server.
- {endpoint} reaches data ({api}) and its only auth signal ({helper}) could not be verified: VibeGuard cannot see inside it. Unverified, so confirm it really authenticates.
- {endpoint} relies on {helper}, but its implementation performs no authentication check, so it reaches data ({api}) unauthenticated.
- {endpoint} modifies data ({api}) without checking the user; only Row Level Security protects it. Verify the policies, and prefer an explicit check.

## How to fix

Authenticate at the start of every handler (or in middleware that provably covers the route), then authorise: check that the user may act on this specific record. Return 401/403 before touching data. Never use a service-role / admin client in a handler that has not verified the caller.

### Vulnerable

```ts
// app/api/notes/[id]/route.ts
export async function DELETE(_req: Request, { params }: { params: { id: string } }) {
  await supabaseAdmin.from('notes').delete().eq('id', params.id); // anyone can delete any note
  return Response.json({ ok: true });
}
```

### Fixed

```ts
export async function DELETE(_req: Request, { params }: { params: { id: string } }) {
  const supabase = await createClient(); // cookie-based, anon key: RLS applies
  const {
    data: { user },
  } = await supabase.auth.getUser();
  if (!user) return new Response('Unauthorized', { status: 401 });
  const { error } = await supabase.from('notes').delete().eq('id', params.id).eq('owner', user.id);
  if (error) return new Response('Forbidden', { status: 403 });
  return Response.json({ ok: true });
}
```

## False positives and limitations

<!-- hand:false-positives -->

False positives are the biggest risk for this rule, so it prefers low confidence over
silence when it cannot decide.

- **Public by design:** public read endpoints (catalogue, published posts, health checks)
  are reported as reads with lower severity. Confirm and suppress with the reason.
- **User-scoped Supabase clients:** a handler that writes through a cookie-based client
  without checking the user is reported at low severity, because RLS is the only guard.
- **Custom auth helpers** that VibeGuard cannot recognise (from a package, behind two levels
  of indirection): list them in `endpoints.authFunctions` once you have confirmed they
  authenticate.
- **Auth at the gateway** (API gateway, Cloudflare Access, Vercel deployment protection,
  reverse proxy with OIDC) is invisible. Suppress with the reason.
- **Routers mounted with auth in another file** (`app.use('/x', auth, router)`) do not
  propagate. Add `router.use(auth)` in the router file, or suppress.
- **Limitations (false negatives):** authorization (may this user act on this record?) is
  not checked; a verified auth call anywhere in the handler counts, even after the write;
  data access deeper than one helper is not seen; dynamically registered routes and other
  frameworks (Hono, NestJS, tRPC, GraphQL) are not discovered.

<!-- /hand:false-positives -->

## How to suppress

Only suppress a finding after confirming it is safe. Put the directive on the line above
the reported line (or use `vibeguard-ignore-line` on the line itself, or
`vibeguard-ignore-file` anywhere in the file). The reason is required: a directive without
one suppresses nothing and is reported.

```ts
// vibeguard-ignore-next-line endpoints/unauthenticated-data-access -- explain why this is safe (at least 10 characters)
<the line VibeGuard reported>
```

Use the comment syntax of the file: `//` or `/* */` in code, `#` in `.env` and YAML
files, `--` in SQL.

To turn the rule off or change its severity for the whole project, use `.vibeguard.yml`:

```yaml
version: 1
rules:
  endpoints/unauthenticated-data-access: off # or: { severity: low }
```

See [configuration](../../configuration.md) and
[ADR-0004](../../adr/0004-suppression-design.md).

## CWE

- [CWE-306](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/306.html): Missing Authentication for Critical Function
- [CWE-862](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/862.html): Missing Authorization
- [CWE-285](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/285.html): Improper Authorization
